introduction: This intermediate tier transitions to the detailed mechanisms of hydrocarbon reactions. It focuses heavily on Free Radical Halogenation, the Anti-Markovnikov addition (Kharasch effect), and the highly-tested oxidative/reductive cleavage of double bonds via Ozonolysis.

core_concepts.title: Free Radical Halogenation of Alkanes
core_concepts.description:
Proceeds via three steps in the presence of UV light ($h\nu$):
1. Initiation: Homolytic cleavage of halogen ($Cl_2 \rightarrow 2Cl^\bullet$).
2. Propagation: $Cl^\bullet + CH_4 \rightarrow HCl + CH_3^\bullet$, followed by $CH_3^\bullet + Cl_2 \rightarrow CH_3Cl + Cl^\bullet$.
3. Termination: Radicals combine ($Cl^\bullet + Cl^\bullet \rightarrow Cl_2$ or $CH_3^\bullet + CH_3^\bullet \rightarrow C_2H_6$).
Reactivity order of halogens: $F_2 > Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2$. Fluorination is dangerously explosive. Iodination is reversible and requires oxidizing agents like $HNO_3$ or $HIO_3$ to push forward.

core_concepts.title: Anti-Markovnikov Addition (Peroxide/Kharasch Effect)
core_concepts.description:
When HBr is added to an unsymmetrical alkene in the presence of organic peroxides ($R-O-O-R$), the addition happens AGAINST Markovnikov's rule. The $Br^\bullet$ radical attaches to the carbon with MORE hydrogens to generate the more stable carbocation/radical intermediate. 
CRITICAL FACT: This effect is strictly limited to HBr. It does NOT work for HCl or HI due to unfavorable thermodynamics in their propagation steps.

core_concepts.title: Ozonolysis of Alkenes
core_concepts.description:
Cleavage of the $C=C$ double bond using Ozone ($O_3$) followed by cleavage of the ozonide intermediate.
1. Reductive Ozonolysis ($O_3$, followed by $Zn/H_2O$ or $DMS$): The double bond breaks cleanly in half. Oxygen atoms cap the broken ends, forming Aldehydes and/or Ketones. (Zinc prevents further oxidation).
2. Oxidative Ozonolysis ($O_3$, followed by $H_2O_2$ or $H_2O$ without $Zn$): Aldehydes are further oxidized into Carboxylic Acids. Ketones remain intact.

core_concepts.title: Hydration of Alkynes (Kucherov Reaction)
core_concepts.description:
Addition of water to an alkyne requires heavy metal catalysis: $HgSO_4 / H_2SO_4$ at $333 \text{ K}$. 
Reaction follows Markovnikov's rule to initially form an unstable 'Enol'. This enol rapidly undergoes tautomerization to form a stable 'Keto' compound. 
Ethyne yields Acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$). ALL other alkynes (e.g., Propyne) yield Ketones (e.g., Acetone).

core_concepts.title: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (EAS) Mechanism
core_concepts.description:
General Mechanism:
1. Generation of Electrophile (e.g., $AlCl_3 + Cl_2 \rightarrow Cl^+ + AlCl_4^-$).
2. Attack of Electrophile on Benzene ring, forming a resonance-stabilized sigma complex (Arenium ion), which temporarily loses aromaticity.
3. Deprotonation: A base removes a proton from the sp3 carbon to restore the aromatic ring.

important_entities.name: Baeyer's Reagent
important_entities.significance: It is the standard chemical test for unsaturation (double/triple bonds). When it reacts with an alkene, it performs a syn-addition of two $-OH$ groups (forming a vicinal diol/glycol). The purple color of $KMnO_4$ disappears, leaving a brown precipitate of $MnO_2$. Alkanes and Benzene do NOT decolorize Baeyer's reagent.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Friedel-Crafts Alkylation (Benzene + $R-Cl$ in anhydrous $AlCl_3$), the introduced alkyl group activates the benzene ring via +I and Hyperconjugation. Thus, the newly formed alkylbenzene is MORE reactive than benzene itself, often leading to unwanted Polyalkylation. To stop at mono-alkylation, use Friedel-Crafts Acylation (introducing an acyl group $-COR$) because the acyl group is powerfully deactivating (-M), preventing further reaction.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Erase the double bond, slap on an Oxygen
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
To rapidly predict reductive ozonolysis products: Draw the alkene, literally erase the two lines of the $C=C$ double bond, and draw an $=O$ at both broken ends. 
Example: $CH_3-CH=C(CH_3)_2 \rightarrow CH_3-CH=O$ (Acetaldehyde) + $O=C(CH_3)_2$ (Acetone).

exam_strategy_tips: In Friedel-Crafts Alkylation, the electrophile is a CARBOCATION. Therefore, it WILL undergo rearrangement (hydride or methyl shift) if it can form a more stable carbocation before attacking the benzene ring. E.g., using 1-chloropropane will yield Isopropylbenzene (Cumene) as the major product, not n-propylbenzene.
